page: Microsoft Azure F1ams_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv7 server family. Powered by a single dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor core on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The CPU includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include local storage, though it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark testing, the single-core architecture delivers top-tier single-threaded performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all rank in the top 10% of tested servers. However, due to the single-vCPU limitation, multi-core and parallelized benchmarks, such as multi-core stress-ng and Passmark CPU scores, fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large blocks and Passmark memory scores remain average, while database operations, Redis SET throughput, and static web serving are relatively weak.

The F1ams_v7 offers a cost-effective entry point for memory-heavy workloads that do not require multi-threaded processing. The high memory density per core makes it qualitatively efficient for lightweight, memory-bound tasks. However, the lack of local storage and the single-core bottleneck represent significant tradeoffs for high-throughput database or web-serving applications. It is best suited for single-threaded background workers, lightweight in-memory caching, small-scale data processing, and basic development or testing environments requiring a dedicated CPU core.
